# Storyfolio

Makes one kind of portfolio site: one long scroll that tells one story, carried by one object in 3D that is taken from the person's own work.

This version plans the site and does not build it. It ends when the person has said yes to a storyboard.

## Three stops

Between stops you work by yourself. At each stop the person decides one thing. You go on only when their answer is in the conversation and you have written it into the file.

| Stop | First open | You put to the person | You go on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Read | `references/reading-a-profile.md` | What you found, as facts to confirm and questions to answer. Nothing else | They have answered, and `docs/story/facts.md` holds their answers |
| 2. Concept | `references/concept.md` | Three concepts, and which you would choose | They have picked one, or told you to pick, and `docs/story/concepts.md` says which |
| 3. Storyboard | `references/storyboard.md` | The script of the whole page | They have said yes to it |

**Your first reply is the first stop, and no more than that.** People ask for the whole plan at once: the idea, the scroll, the colours. Do not give it yet, and say why in a sentence. A plan made now is made from your reading of a resume, and a resume leaves out exactly what a site must not get wrong: whose result a number was, what a title hides, who took a photograph. Once they have answered you will have a better idea, and it will not have to be taken apart.

When the storyboard has its yes, say that building is not in this version, and bring `docs/story/handover.md` up to date.

## Ask or decide

Ask the person when a thing is:

1. a fact only they know,
2. a claim that could embarrass them if it were wrong,
3. taste on what a visitor sees first: the concept, the look, the opening words,
4. anything that publishes, costs money, or shows another person or an employer's work.

Everything else you decide. Write each decision into `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: what you decided, why, and how to change it.

If the person will not answer, or tells you to decide everything, open `references/asking.md`.

## What you keep

In the person's own folder, so that a later session can go on from the files alone:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/story/facts.md` | The fact sheet, each fact with where it came from, and the person's answers |
| `docs/story/concepts.md` | The three concepts, which was picked, and why |
| `docs/story/storyboard.md` | The script |
| `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` | What you decided without asking |
| `docs/story/handover.md` | What exists, what the person has said, what is next |

## What holds from the first stop on

- **Nothing about the person is invented.** You know that a number, an employer, a title and a quote are facts. So is every small thing a sentence says on its way: what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used, which came first, why, how a thing was left, what it taught them. That sounds like writing, and it is a claim. Before handing over any reply or file, check each claim against the fact sheet, including introductory summaries, working titles and labels on the object's faces. Read the supporting line and its unresolved questions, not just its reference. It must establish the whole claim: a topic attached to one item does not establish the topic of another. Wording that depends on an unanswered question stays out of the introduction and the planned page, even if copied from a profile. Remove it or list it as a question to confirm.
- **A number is used as the person confirmed it,** with what it measures and whose result it is.
- **What is someone else's is asked about before it is planned for:** a photograph a photographer took, a friend's drawing, a quote, an employer's screens, a story with a patient or a client in it.

# Storyfolio engine

A starting project for one scroll, one story and one family of 3D pieces.
The supplied page is a plain test story, not a person's portfolio.

Taken from V3 at `163b8ceb302b7b4e5beeff8f1161f4cdc7663b15` and made
independent of that site's content, paper shapes and assets. The source
project is unchanged. Storyfolio's engine and generated SVGs are MIT licensed.

## Start

Use Node 22.18 or later with native TypeScript support. Scaffold this folder
with `node <installed-skill>/scripts/scaffold.mjs <site-folder>`. Existing
`docs/story/` files are kept; any conflicting engine path aborts the copy.
Then, in the new site folder:

```bash
npm ci
npm run browsers
npm run dev
```

Open the local address printed by Next.js. Append `?look=dark` to choose a
look and `?fps` to show the frame meter. The appearance switch preserves
other query parameters, the fragment and the current scroll position.
Read the frame meter on a real phone; software rendering in a headless
browser does not measure phone performance.

Never install dependencies inside an installed skill. The copied project
belongs to the person, has its own lockfile, and does not depend on the
skill after scaffolding. System fonts make builds independent of remote
font services. Add licensed local files with `next/font/local` if needed;
the scene starts without waiting for them and redraws faces when fonts load.

## From storyboard to content

`lib/story/` contains pure, tested calculations. `components/story/` owns
the browser and scene. The person's story belongs in `content/`:

| File | Storyboard input |
|---|---|
| `story.ts` | Chapter IDs, names, roles, beat IDs and screen heights; one fixed piece count |
| `formations.ts` | A rest formation for every beat; optional `within` formation reached as its rest is scrolled |
| `faces.ts` | Pictures or canvas drawing functions for a beat and piece |
| `copy.ts` | Metadata, language, labels and complete HTML text |
| `looks.ts` | Ground, text and surface colors, lights and matte/no floor |
| `extras.ts` | Lazy imports of chapter-specific shapes, each in its own error boundary |
| `links.ts` | Ordinary HTML links over a named piece at a named beat |
| `checks.json` | Optional checks of capabilities this fixture exercises |

Use `as const satisfies StoryDef` for the story and
`satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>` for formations. `checkStory`
also rejects invalid IDs, heights, piece counts and face references at
runtime. A formation contains one position, rotation and size per piece,
plus framing. `layouts.ts` supplies stack, fan, ring, grid, row and seeded
scatter; `measure` bounds their rotated faces. Depth, a custom shape's
extent and a whole formation's turn can require extra framing room.

The HTML in `app/page.tsx` follows the same beat order using `Chapter` and
`Beat`. A `Beat` can carry a static `fallback` image or diagram. Keep one
`h1`, stable chapter heading IDs and every factual claim in HTML. The check
script verifies the rendered beat IDs against the content contract.

The bundle type is in `components/story/types.ts`. Import a bundle inside a
client component, as `content/experience.tsx` does, and pass server-rendered
HTML as children. Bundles contain drawing functions and component loaders,
so cannot be serialized across a server/client prop boundary.

A custom `Piece` component receives its index, face material and look.
Build it at unit width/height centered at the origin. Its parent group gets
the formation's position, rotation and width/height scale each frame. Keep
materials present from the first frame. Extras receive the shared frame,
look, reduced-motion flag and control store and mount only near their
chapter. Their shapes are children of the formation group.

Use `useExtraFrame` from `components/story/extra-frame.tsx` for an extra's
frame callback. It receives the same state, delta and optional XR frame as
React Three Fiber's `useFrame`. A synchronous exception disables that
callback immediately and unmounts its owning extra, leaving the core scene,
other extras and HTML running. Each extra also has a React boundary for
render failures and rejected lazy imports. For example:

```tsx
useExtraFrame(() => {
  if (line.current) line.current.visible = frameRef.current.from === 1;
});
```

`content/extras/middle-line.tsx` uses this hook. A raw third-party `useFrame`
callback, timer, event handler or rejected asynchronous task does not pass
through this guard. Handle failures at those boundaries explicitly;
wrapping a component in a React boundary does not catch them.

For caption controls, use `useControl` or `useControls` from
`components/story/controls.tsx` in a client component. Real controls remain
HTML. The canvas takes no pointer events. Overlay links are hidden and
removed from keyboard navigation outside their beat; supply the same
destination in the text for fallback access.

For a sketch, add a client component importing its own bundle and HTML to
`content/sketches/index.ts`. Its key becomes `/sketch/<id>`. The initial
registry is empty and unknown keys return 404.

## Check

```bash
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run check
```

`check` builds, starts its own production server on a free local port,
runs the browser matrix and stops only that process group. It writes a
manifest, logs, reports and screenshots under `checks/<timestamp>/` and
returns a failure exit code for failed checks. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`
selects an optional shared browser cache. `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE` is an optional
override; normally the installed local package provides the browser tool.

The matrix checks both looks at wide, short and phone sizes, reduced
motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript. Optional plain-story probes exercise
keyboard access and failed chapter loading. Context loss checks the HTML
fallback. Wide captures include the beginning, middle and end of each
beat's rest; reduced-motion captures also check that a stationary scene
stays still. Open every screenshot for overlap, clipping, legibility and
framing. Automatic passes do not replace visual review.

For a focused investigation use `npm run check -- --only=light-phone`.
`--skip-build` checks a previously built app and is diagnostic only.
Neither establishes a fresh full acceptance run. `scripts/shoot.mjs`
documents individual screenshots, blocked requests, look switching,
overflow and shader checks.

No JavaScript leaves the server-rendered text. No WebGL or a failed scene
leaves ordinary text and any beat's static image. Reduced motion cuts
between poses, including within-beat formations, without idle movement.
The scene pauses offscreen, caps sharpness on touch devices and steps down
quality when measured frames stay slow.
# Working on this site

Read `docs/story/handover.md` first, if it exists. Keep it current with the
person's words, decisions, implementation and check results. Keep all
lasting context in this repository and commit it with the work.

This starter uses Next.js 16. Before using an unfamiliar API, read the
relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` if provided by the installed
package, otherwise consult the official Next.js documentation for that
version. Do not assume older examples apply.

Install dependencies with `npm ci`, install Chromium with `npm run browsers`,
then run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run check`.
The last command builds and checks a production server. Open its screenshots
before calling a visual change done. Read `README.md` for the content
contract and where the results are written.

The plain story is a test of the engine. Replace it from the person's
approved storyboard and confirmed facts. Keep the text complete without
the scene, and test reduced motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript.
# State by state: amended build storyboard

Approved fictional derivative for `embedded-1`, 11 October 2026. The

## Governing idea

**How does a firmware decision become a measurable signal?** A state table
becomes a responsibility table, an explanatory diagram and an evidence
ledger, then returns to a complete table. Six persistent matte row cards
carry the story. They are narrative pieces, not six firmware states or six
physical boards. This is a card-engine fixture, not a non-sheet proof.

The audience is a firmware hiring manager. State Ada's contribution and
its limits clearly in HTML. The scene supplements that text. The colleague's
PCB/analogue contribution stays distinct from Ada's firmware, scheduling
and fixture work; measured inputs, projected endurance and unfinished
qualification stay distinct from one another.

## Chapters and beats

Use these stable chapter and beat IDs. Each chapter contains a corresponding
semantic section and heading. Each beat uses the engine's `data-beat`
attribute. The heading for `scope.opening` is the page's single h1.

| Chapter ID and label | Beat ID and heading | Desktop screens | Formation and HTML content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scope`, Scope | `scope.opening`, Ada Mensah | 1 | Six flat rows gain shallow depth. Name, question, firmware meaning, contribution and the explicitly explanatory fixture preview. Contact and CV available immediately. |
| `responsibilities`, Responsibilities | `responsibilities.split`, Who made what | 1 | Same rows separate into clearly attributed groups. Exact Ada and colleague contribution sentences from confirmations 3 and 4. |
| `state`, State | `state.table`, Scheduling power states | 1 | Rows align as a ruled table. Explain state tables as a daily working document and scheduling as part of Ada's confirmed contribution. Do not claim actual state-machine entries. |
| `transition`, Transition | `transition.diagram`, Reading transitions | 1.5 | Rows form the supplied explanatory Sleep, Measure, Transmit loop. Keep its teaching-diagram limit visible using sentence 9. No timing/current values, invented branches or incident fix. Link to the SVG at readable size. |
| `observation`, Observation | `observation.fixture`, Checking basic operation | 1 | Shallow bench review with the fixture schematic prominent. Use bring-up definition, sentence 2, and explanatory limit, sentence 10. Link to the SVG at readable size. |
| `observation`, Observation | `observation.evidence`, What the bench supports | 1.5 | Evidence ledger. Sentences 5, 6, 7 and 8 preserve assembled/tested/customer status, projection, longest run and unfinished qualification. Never imply the 72-hour run validated two years. |
| `review`, Review | `review.close`, Code beside evidence | 1 | Rows reassemble into the opening table. Use closing answer, sentence 11, alongside the evidence limits; repeat email and downloadable corrected CV. |

Approximate desktop budget: eight viewport lengths. Static mobile height
follows readable content; do not retain eight empty desktop scroll screens.
Content must stay available after arriving at every beat, including both
beats in Observation. Every exact core sentence must be in visible HTML,
not only a card texture, aria label or hidden fallback.

## Spine review at stop 4

Build the opening, Transition from the middle, and Review first. Offer
Bench paper, Instrument paper and Review sheet as three appearances of
the same object and story. The person picks a look by scrolling. The rest
of the body need not be complete until stop 5. Do not fabricate approval.

## Look and motion

| Look | Ground | Ink | Accent | Card surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bench paper | Warm off-white | Graphite | Muted amber | Matte cream, fine ruled lines |
| Instrument paper | Deep graphite | Pale ivory | Muted amber | Dark matte, fine pale rules |
| Review sheet | Cool light grey | Charcoal | Restrained blue | Light grey, restrained annotations |

Bench paper starts as the default. System sans-serif prose and monospace
notation replace the two unsupplied named font families in the historical
plan. All looks must preserve contrast, meaning and readable evidence
labels. No glossy circuitry, sci-fi display or measured-looking waveform.

Normal desktop scroll drives short translations and rotations of the same
six cards. Stable rests, no forced horizontal movement, autoplay or
scroll hijacking. Keep the camera steady except modest diagram framing.
Chapter links jump to the correct content; settled scene state must agree
with deep links. Complete text never depends on a face being visible.

## Static modes and accessibility

At widths of 767 CSS pixels or less, use a single-column static page with
chapter anchors and large readable supplied diagrams. Do not mount or
download a scene-only/WebGL chunk to read this mode. At wider widths with
reduced-motion preference, use the same static content with no scene
canvas or scroll-driven movement. These are explicit fixture choices that
override the engine's default mobile and reduced-motion animation behavior.

No JavaScript, unavailable WebGL and a renderer failure all retain the
complete seven-beat HTML, diagrams, navigation, email and CV. A CSS-hidden
or invisible animated canvas is not the chosen static mode. A desktop
without those constraints must have the intended scene.

There is one h1 and unique IDs for both Observation beats. Meaning is not
encoded by color alone. Images have the alternative text recorded in
`assets.md`, diagram descriptions are ordinary HTML, links work with the
keyboard and focus remains visible. A simple link to each SVG is the
approved keyboard-operable expansion; no dialog or complex zoom is needed.

## Navigation and required link labels

A compact header offers `Email Ada` (`mailto:ada@example.com`), `Download
CV` (`/ada-mensah-cv.html`, with download behavior), and `Skip to contact`
(`#review`). Repeat email and CV in Review. Keep all six chapter anchors
reachable, as well as skip-to-content. At the relevant beats use `View
power-state schematic` (`/assets/power-states.svg`) and `View fixture
schematic` (`/assets/bring-up-fixture.svg`).

The page metadata identifies Ada Mensah and firmware work. English is the
document language. The supplied share SVG and icon are illustrative local
assets; using them does not prove social platforms accept SVG previews.
State that support limit in the final handover instead of asserting a
tested cross-platform card. If the build converts the share card to a
supported raster format locally, record that derivative and keep its source.

## Copy, scope and finish

At stop 5 draft the surrounding prose from `facts.md` and show choices for
the key opening and closing wording. Retain the eleven confirmed sentences
and seven fixed headings. They are part of the fixture's acceptance
contract, not measurements or externally validated project claims.

Every site-checklist decision is recorded in `decided-for-you.md`.
Mosslink's one complete case stays on the main page. A missing-address page
has a Home link and email; legal details remain a prepublication task.

At stop 6 check all three looks, normal desktop, static phone, reduced
motion, JavaScript/WebGL failures, keyboard navigation, deep links,
contact/CV links, all assets, and missing-route behavior. Record commands,
results and limitations in the project. A scripted fictional approval
cannot stand in for the real repository author's scrolling review.
# Fictional confirmations for this build

## Core wording to keep in readable HTML

The following sentences are approved for this fictional derivative. Keep
them verbatim in the relevant beat's visible HTML so the coordinator can
check the factual contract independently. Draft headings, transitions and
surrounding prose at stop 5 without adding unsupported claims. The fixed
headings in the storyboard identify beats and are also part of this case.

2. Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation.
3. I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture.

PCB, deployed a customer pilot, measured two years of battery endurance,

description: Enable fast client-side navigation with the built-in `next/link` component.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

`<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.

Basic usage:

<AppOnly>

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Page() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher

export default function Page() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

</AppOnly>

```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function Home() {
  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
}
```

```jsx filename="pages/index.js" switcher
import Link from 'next/link'

  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
```
